messages:
perf-bot: Canary perf regression detected on canary-3 (release/2026-03-10): p50 +22% vs baseline, increased tail and CPU. Auto-tagged: kernel-selection, kv-cache

mike: saw the alert. can we confirm scope? which model & seq dist?

jordan: deploy-bot shows release id = r2026-03-10-14d, canary only. no other services touched. rolling hold applied.

alice: FYI I merged PR #4123 yesterday (tokenizer -> trim trailing spaces + pad-to-multiple-of-8 default change). small change but touches seq length distribution.

sara: running quick repro locally against canary build. collecting perf profile now (short seq workload).

mike: quick grep of serving logs shows kernel_selection fallback rate jumped:
```
kernel_selection_stats: { fast_kernel: 0.78, generic_attention: 0.22 }
prev-baseline: { fast_kernel: 0.94, generic_attention: 0.06 }
```
looks like more tokens are landing in generic_attention, which is ~3-4x slower for our HW path.

sara: also KV cache hit ratio for short queries dropped: 92% -> 61%. evict churn higher. full flamegraph attached (link) but top hot path = generic_attention + memcpy.

mike: starting bisect. git bisect start HEAD good@r2026-03-09 bad@r2026-03-10 && git bisect run ./scripts/perf_gate_check.sh (local perf harness: shortseq-1000 iters).

alice: if bisect points to my tokenizer PR I'll open revert. odd that pad-to-multiple-of-8 would change kernel selection that much but sequence length distribution shift makes sense.

perf-bot: bisect finished -> culprit: commit 9f3b2e1 (tokenizer: pad-to-multiple-of-8 default).

jordan: thanks. we should revert in canary and make a hotfix. is there a safer transform (pad only for long seqs) we can land?

mike: short-term plan: revert commit from canary (hotfix revert PR) + add CI perf test that asserts kernel selection ratios and KV-hit > 85% for shortseq workload. long-term: make kernel selector robust to small seq-distribution shifts (prefer fast_kernel for borderline lengths).

alice: opening PR for revert and test. PR: https://git/repo/pulls/1267 (revert + perf test). includes a unit test simulating padding behavior and an integration check that runs in perf-nightly.

sara: added a targeted micro-benchmark to perf-harness: shortseq-kv-hit-check. will add threshold to perf-gate: p50 <= baseline*1.10 and kv_hit >= 0.85. also adding test retry to reduce flakiness.

mike: posted a short patch to kernel selector to bias toward fast_kernel when selection score within 7% margin. will run canary with bias flag off by default, toggle via rollout.

deploy-bot: rollout hold removed for canary after manual revert merged (r2026-03-10-hotfix). canary redeploy started at 2026-03-10T15:10Z.

jordan: monitoring canary now. if p50 back to baseline for 30m we can promote.

perf-bot: canary metrics update: p50 back to +3% after revert, kv_hit 90%.

alice: created follow-up task: add a perf unit in pre-merge CI that simulates tokenizer edge-case and asserts kernel_selection distribution. ticket #PROJ-789.

mike: follow-ups: (1) tighten perf-gate thresholds for nightlies, (2) instrument kernel-selection telemetry (histograms + flags), (3) investigate KV eviction policy sensitivity for short-living entries.

sara: I'll land the perf-gate changes and add a retry/stabilization window to reduce noisy failures. also adding a small smoke perf-run to PR checks for changes touching tokenizer or kernel selector.

jordan: retrospective notes: small functional changes that alter sequence-length distribution can have outsized perf impacts. we need a checklist for API/SDK/text changes: add perf regressions check + perf test docs.

mike: agreed. will draft a short doc and a pre-merge checklist item.

alice: thanks everyone. assigning owners: mike (kernel selector bias + telemetry), sara (perf-gate + benchmarks), alice (tokenizer revert test + doc), jordan (canary monitoring + rollout policy).

jordan: closing loop — canary stable for 2h, promoting to prod this afternoon. :tada:

mike: noted: let's keep the new kernel bias behind a feature flag until we have more perf-signal across models.

sara: will follow up with nightly metric dump and a short retro doc with graphs.

perf-bot: CI perf-gate result: PR 1267 passed perf-gate after revert (no regressions).
